Nissan Celebrates 20 Years of Qashqai With Funky-Retro Y2K Livery and a Qashqai Heritage Collection
23 photos
Photo: Nissan
Actually, the Nissan Qashqai Heritage Collection isn't a new special edition or even some accessories or apparel collection - it's just a digital archive that chronicles the model's design and innovation history.
Nissan is making some interesting connections these days. For example, in America, the Japanese automaker has decided to mark the special occasion of Nissan Patrol's 75th anniversary in the United States, too, by launching the 2027 Nissan Armada Patrol PRO-4X trim level complete with a few novelties.
Moving to Europe , Nissan Qashqai celebrates 20 years since its 2006 debut at the 2006 Paris Motor Show in France, with the brand often credited with “the creation of the compact crossover blueprint” following its introduction. It’s always been an Old Continent-focused product, with more than 4.1 million units delivered to Europe, but the Qashqai has also registered about half a million sales for global markets during its two-decade tenure.
Today, the Nissan Qashqai is sold in more than 100 countries and has received over 110 international accolades, and the latest version - Qashqai with Nissan e‑POWER hybrid technology – has already reached 250k European customers. Naturally, the brand wanted to mark the occasion of its 20th anniversary and created a bespoke 'Y2K' livery and the Qashqai Heritage Collection.
Back in the early 2000s, buyers of conventional European family cars usually chose between a hatchback, a sedan, a station wagon, a minivan or a true SUV . Nissan's European teams wanted to be different and, instead of bringing a new Almera hatchback to life, went with “a new style of vehicle that combined the best attributes of several categories: the compact footprint, practicality, affordability, simplicity and efficiency of a family hatchback with the robust styling and raised seating position of an SUV.”
The Nissan Qashqai became an instant success with 100k units delivered in just nine months, and Nissan sold one million units by January 2011. Today, the model has reached its third generation since 2021 and was refreshed in 2024, with the e-Power hybrid launched in late 2022 with 157 combined hp and a combined fuel economy of up to 4.3 L/100 km (54.7 mpg), with a maximum range of 1,279 km (795 miles) from a full tank (WLTP), and sprinting to 100 kph or 62 mph in 7.6 seconds.
To mark the occasion of the anniversary, a digital artist and creator called Dale (Heymoonly) Lendl created a unique 'sticker bomb' design with Nissan. The Y2K-style livery “reinterprets early-2000s visual culture through a contemporary lens, using the vibrant neon palette and digital-art influences to celebrate Qashqai's disruptive origins.”
The car was also customized inside and has “fun accessories” like velour seat covers, a colorful steering wheel cover, pop CDs from the era, and even “a functional iPod complete with a mid-2000s playlist.” Cool, right?
